claim: Pooled nudge effect in the published literature is d about 0.43-0.45 unadjusted, with extreme heterogeneity (I2 99.7%, about 15% of interventions predicted to backfire).
agent_test: Report per-task-family effects with intervals, never a single pooled scaffold gain.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Publication bias is real in the nudge literature: Egger b about 2.1-2.3, funnel asymmetry, and the original authors concede it.
agent_test: Count only scaffold gains measured on preregistered, held-out items.

claim: After bias correction the average nudge effect shrinks to near zero (d -0.01 to 0.12) with wide intervals; the data cannot rule out a small true effect.
agent_test: Compare scaffold gain on exploratory vs fresh held-out items; expect shrinkage.

claim: Structure nudges (defaults, effort) are the strongest category (d 0.55 raw); after correction still undecided (RoBMA 0.12) while information and assistance nudges show evidence against an effect (BF01 up to 34).
agent_test: Test structural scaffold changes (forced format, defaults) vs advice-style prompt additions at equal tokens.

claim: Domain moderates effects: food largest raw (d 0.72), finance smallest and strongly null after correction.
agent_test: Evaluate scaffold per task type; do not pool.

claim: At-scale nudge-unit trials (126 RCTs, 23.5M people) show 1.4 pp, about one sixth of academic published nudges (8.7 pp); low power plus selective publication explain most of the gap.
agent_test: Re-run each kept scaffold gain on a larger fresh sample; expect large shrinkage if selected on small samples.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Experts and forecasters overpredict nudge and intervention effects; megastudy judges cannot pick winners.
agent_test: Do not let the agent or an LLM judge rank its own scaffold ideas; measure.

claim: Megastudies show real but small gains and winner's curse: 19 vaccine texts avg +2.1 pp (best 4.6, shrunk 2.8); 22 flu texts +2.0 pp; savings email +0.05 pp; gym effects persist for only 8%.
agent_test: Run many scaffold variants in one shared benchmark and shrink the winner's estimate.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Effects rarely transfer across settings; ideas that win in surveys or expert ratings often fail in the field.
agent_test: Validate scaffold transfer across model and task before keeping.

claim: Defaults work best but vary (d 0.68 over 58 studies; some null or negative); auto-enrolment moved participation from about half to 86% but anchored contributions at 3%. Three firms: participation above 85%, but after three years half still sat at the 2-3% default rate and conservative fund, offsetting the wealth gain on average (abstract only).
agent_test: Defaults in the prompt (format, effort) may help; check side effects on the unchosen dimensions.

claim: LLMs follow irrelevant defaults, suggestions and social cues well beyond human rates (Cherep, Halimeh, Montero-Porras: three groups). Stronger reasoning lowers default following only partly (92% to 86%) and can raise social-cue following (96% to 98%).
agent_test: Probe the agent with irrelevant defaults and wrong suggestions; measure acceptance rate.

claim: In shopping agents, defaults raise odds 8.7x and social proof 37x; high reasoning halves default following but raises social-proof following. Full text re-read: OR 8.70 and 37.24 confirmed; default OR 0.51 and social OR 1.71 under high reasoning; size-class pattern is exploratory.
agent_test: Test whether a deliberate reflection step cuts default pull without raising social/authority cue pull.

claim: LLM choices depend on prompt wording and format more than on model: a rewording flips rejection to fixation of a bad default (0.27 to 0.88), and format alone moves accuracy by up to 76 points (median 6-8) with weak transfer between models.
agent_test: Run each scaffold under 3 paraphrases; report spread.

claim: Chain of thought and few-shot human examples shift choices but do not remove nudge hypersensitivity.
agent_test: Measure default-following with and without CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Pre-revealing information chosen by a resource-rational model raises payoffs of humans and several LLMs, with no human data.
agent_test: Test an information-presentation scaffold selected by a cost-benefit rule.

claim: Instruction tuning and RLHF amplify cognitive biases (decoy, framing, omission) in LLMs; base models show less.
agent_test: Run bias probes on the target model before relying on its intuition.

claim: LLMs reproduce classic behavioural effects qualitatively (status quo, anchoring, framing), but size is unreliable and simulated humans are distorted (r=0.20).
agent_test: Do not use the agent as a simulated user to size effects.

claim: Explicit debiasing prompts help partly (self-help debiasing best) but biases persist even when the optimal formula is supplied.
agent_test: Test a debiasing-instruction step at equal tokens on framing items.

claim: LLM-generated nudges in the field have small or mixed results: personalised energy nudges -0.56 kWh/room-day; rewritten vaccine messages no overall gain; news bots small.
agent_test: Measure rewritten prompts against originals on blind held-out items.

claim: Agent-loop guidance reduces visible misbehaviour (90.9% judged recovered after one intervention; 79.1% after several) but the live A/B effects are small (tool failures -4.2%, tokens -5.3%) and task accuracy was not measured.
agent_test: Test mid-run guidance injection vs none at equal tokens, scored on held-out task accuracy, not on loops avoided.

claim: Failures to replicate may reflect real context dependence, so evidence must be gathered per context.
agent_test: Report scaffold effect by task type and model.

claim: Advice-style prompt additions (think step by step) give small average gains on non-reasoning models against a no-thinking control, near-zero against the model default, and marginal or negative gains on reasoning models; the exact wording of the advice barely matters.
agent_test: Compare scaffold variants against the model default at equal tokens, not against an answer-directly control.

claim: LLM judges can rank experimental treatments well (r about 0.85 on survey experiments) but overestimate effect sizes, and correlation falls on megastudies to expert-forecaster level; human experts also fail at rank-ordering treatments.
agent_test: Let the agent rank scaffold variants, then score ranking against measured results; never replace measurement.

claim: Gaps 1, 2 and 3 are untested by anyone for scaffolds: no study compares structural vs advice scaffold changes at equal tokens on fresh items with shrinkage, and none tests whether an agent can forecast which variant wins.
agent_test: Run it in our own harness: split items into exploratory and fresh sets, shrink the winner, forecast before measuring.

claim: Gaps 6 and 9 (debiasing at equal tokens; preregistered structure-nudge trials) were not searched successfully in this pass because of rate limits; they remain open, not negative.
agent_test: Retry searches when budget returns.
